questions.question: What is the full name of the POSH Act?
questions.answer: The Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013.

questions.question: Who is an "Aggrieved Woman" under the Act?
questions.answer: A woman of any age, whether employed or not, who alleges to have been subjected to any act of sexual harassment by the respondent.

questions.question: Does the Act protect men?
questions.answer: The Act is gender-specific for women, but many organizations have gender-neutral internal policies.

questions.question: Is a "Domestic Worker" covered under POSH?
questions.answer: Yes, the Act specifically includes domestic workers in dwelling places.

questions.question: What are the five categories of "unwelcome acts" defined in Section 2(n)?
questions.answer: (i) Physical contact/advances, (ii) Demand for sexual favors, (iii) Sexually colored remarks, (iv) Showing pornography, (v) Any other unwelcome physical/verbal/non-verbal conduct of a sexual nature.

questions.question: Define "Quid Pro Quo" harassment.
questions.answer: "This for that"—promising work benefits (promotion, raise) in exchange for sexual favors.

questions.question: Define "Hostile Work Environment."
questions.answer: Creating an intimidating or offensive atmosphere that interferes with a woman's work performance.

questions.question: Is an intern considered an "employee"?
questions.answer: Yes, interns (paid or unpaid), trainees, and apprentices are all covered.

questions.question: Does "Workplace" include a company-provided bus or cab?
questions.answer: Yes, transportation provided by the employer for the journey to/from work is an "extended workplace."

questions.question: What about a hotel room during a business trip?
questions.answer: Yes, any place visited by the employee arising out of or during the course of employment is a workplace.

questions.question: Is "unwelcome" the same as "non-consensual"?
questions.answer: "Unwelcome" is broader; even if a woman doesn't say "no" out of fear, the act can still be unwelcome.

questions.question: Can a woman file a complaint against another woman?
questions.answer: Yes, the law allows for a woman to be the "respondent."

questions.question: Is a one-time incident enough to be harassment?
questions.answer: Yes, a single severe incident can constitute sexual harassment.

questions.question: What is the "Impact vs. Intent" rule?
questions.answer: The harasser’s intent doesn't matter; the law focuses on the impact on the aggrieved woman.

questions.question: Are contractual or daily-wage workers covered?
questions.answer: Yes, the definition of employee is highly inclusive.

questions.question: Is a client or a vendor considered a "Respondent"?
questions.answer: Yes, if they harass an employee at the workplace.

questions.question: Does the Act apply to NGOs and hospitals?
questions.answer: Yes, it applies to all private and public sector organizations.

questions.question: Can "staring" be considered sexual harassment?
questions.answer: Yes, it falls under "non-verbal conduct of a sexual nature."

questions.question: Are "sexually colored remarks" limited to spoken words?
questions.answer: No, it includes texts, emails, and social media comments.

questions.question: Is an office holiday party considered a workplace?
questions.answer: Yes, if it is organized or funded by the employer.

questions.question: Does the Act apply to the "Unorganized Sector"?
questions.answer: Yes, through the Local Committee (LC).

questions.question: What is an "Ad-hoc" employee?
questions.answer: Someone employed on a temporary or casual basis; they are fully protected.

questions.question: Can a student in a school/college be an "Aggrieved Woman"?
questions.answer: Yes, the Act covers students and researchers in educational institutions.

questions.question: Define "Sexual Harassment" in 3 words.
questions.answer: Unwelcome sexual conduct.

questions.question: Is "interference with work" a criterion for harassment?
questions.answer: Yes, if it creates an intimidating environment.

questions.question: What is the minimum number of members in an IC?
questions.answer: Four.

questions.question: Who must be the Presiding Officer (PO) of the IC?
questions.answer: A woman employed at a senior level at the workplace.

questions.question: How many members of the IC must be women?
questions.answer: At least one-half (50%) of the total members.

questions.question: What is the role of the "External Member"?
questions.answer: To ensure impartiality and bring expertise from an NGO or legal background.

questions.question: What is the maximum tenure of an IC member?
questions.answer: Three years from the date of their nomination.

questions.question: Can the IC exist without an External Member?
questions.answer: No, the committee would be considered illegally constituted.

questions.question: What is a "Quorum" for an IC meeting?
questions.answer: A minimum of three members, including the Presiding Officer.

questions.question: Does the IC have the powers of a Civil Court?
questions.answer: Yes, under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.

questions.question: Can an IC member be removed before 3 years?
questions.answer: Yes, if they breach confidentiality or are convicted of an offense.

questions.question: What happens if a company has multiple branches?
questions.answer: An IC must be constituted at all administrative units or offices.

questions.question: Are IC members paid for their work?
questions.answer: External members are entitled to an allowance/fees; internal members usually perform it as part of their duty.

questions.question: Can an HR Head be the Presiding Officer?
questions.answer: Yes, provided she is a senior-level woman employee.

questions.question: Is the IC responsible for "Prevention" or just "Redressal"?
questions.answer: Both; they must also organize awareness programs.

questions.question: Can the IC initiate an inquiry without a written complaint?
questions.answer: No, a written complaint is a mandatory trigger.

questions.question: What is the IC’s power regarding witnesses?
questions.answer: They can summon any person and examine them on oath.

questions.question: Who appoints the IC members?
questions.answer: The Employer, through an order in writing.

questions.question: Can a male employee be a member of the IC?
questions.answer: Yes, as long as the 50% women requirement is met.

questions.question: Is training for IC members mandatory?
questions.answer: Yes, the employer must provide skill-building and training for IC members.

questions.question: What if the PO is the one being accused?
questions.answer: She must recuse herself, and a new senior woman must be appointed as PO for that case.

questions.question: Can the IC demand documents from the Respondent?
questions.answer: Yes, they have the power to require the discovery and production of documents.

questions.question: What is "Conflict of Interest" in an IC?
questions.answer: When a member has a personal or professional relationship with a party that might bias their judgment.

questions.question: Does the IC report to the HR department?
questions.answer: No, the IC is an independent body that submits reports to the Employer.

questions.question: Can an external member be a lawyer?
questions.answer: Yes, often they are lawyers or social workers familiar with POSH.

questions.question: What is the "District Officer's" role in IC?
questions.answer: The IC submits an Annual Report to the District Officer.

questions.question: Can an IC member be sued for their decisions?
questions.answer: Generally, they are protected if they act in "good faith" as per the Act.

questions.question: What is the time limit for filing a complaint?
questions.answer: Within 3 months from the date of the incident (or the last incident in a series).

questions.question: Can the 3-month timeline be extended?
questions.answer: Yes, the IC can extend it by another 3 months if they are satisfied with the reasons for the delay.

questions.question: Does the complaint need to be in writing?
questions.answer: Yes, 6 copies of the written complaint along with supporting documents/witness names are required.

questions.question: What if the woman cannot write?
questions.answer: The IC is legally bound to provide "all reasonable assistance" to help her put the complaint in writing.

questions.question: Can a friend or relative file the complaint?
questions.answer: Yes, if the woman is physically or mentally incapacitated, or in case of her death.

questions.question: Are anonymous complaints valid?
questions.answer: No, the Act requires a signed complaint. However, the IC can use an anonymous tip to conduct "general awareness" sessions.

questions.question: Can a complaint be filed via email?
questions.answer: Yes, most ICs accept digital complaints, which are then formalized.

questions.question: Must the complaint name specific witnesses?
questions.answer: It is highly recommended to include witness names and contact details at the time of filing.

questions.question: What should the complaint include?
questions.answer: Dates, times, location, details of the incident, and name of the respondent.

questions.question: Is there a fee for filing a POSH complaint?
questions.answer: No, the process is free for the aggrieved woman.

questions.question: Can a complaint be filed after leaving the company?
questions.answer: Yes, as long as it is within the 3-month limitation period.

questions.question: Who can file if the woman is deceased?
questions.answer: Her legal heir or any person with knowledge of the incident (with the heir's consent).

questions.question: What is a "Nodal Officer"?
questions.answer: A person designated by the District Officer to receive complaints in the unorganized sector.

questions.question: Can the IC refuse a complaint?
questions.answer: Only if it doesn't fall under "Sexual Harassment" or is outside their jurisdiction.

questions.question: What is the first step the IC takes after receiving a complaint?
questions.answer: They must send a copy of the complaint to the Respondent within 7 working days.

questions.question: How long does the Respondent have to reply?
questions.answer: 10 working days from the date of receiving the complaint copy.

questions.question: Can a complaint be filed against a former employee?
questions.answer: Yes, if the incident occurred while they were employed.

questions.question: What if the harasser is a Senior Executive?
questions.answer: The process remains the same; the IC’s independence is protected by law.

questions.question: Can a woman file a police complaint (FIR) simultaneously?
questions.answer: Yes, the internal inquiry and a criminal case can run parallelly.

questions.question: Does "mental incapacity" include trauma?
questions.answer: Yes, if a psychiatrist/psychologist certifies the woman is unable to file herself.

questions.question: How long does the IC have to complete an inquiry?
questions.answer: 90 days.

questions.question: What is "Natural Justice"?
questions.answer: Ensuring both sides are heard fairly and the IC remains unbiased.

questions.question: Can the parties bring lawyers to the hearing?
questions.answer: No, legal practitioners are strictly barred from representing parties in IC proceedings.

questions.question: What is the standard of proof used by the IC?
questions.answer: "Preponderance of Probability" (What is more likely to have happened).

questions.question: What happens if a party misses 3 consecutive hearings?
questions.answer: The IC can terminate the inquiry or pass an "Ex-parte" decision (decide without them).

questions.question: Can the IC interview witnesses privately?
questions.answer: No, the principles of natural justice require that evidence be shared with both parties.

questions.question: What is "Interim Relief"?
questions.answer: Temporary measures like transferring the respondent or granting the woman 3 months of paid leave.

questions.question: Are IC proceedings open to the public?
questions.answer: No, they are strictly confidential and held "In-camera."

questions.question: Can the IC record the audio/video of the hearing?
questions.answer: Yes, but only for internal record-keeping and with the consent of those involved.

questions.question: What is the "Right to Cross-Examination"?
questions.answer: The respondent's right to challenge the complainant’s testimony (usually done through written questions to avoid direct confrontation).

questions.question: Can the IC summon people from outside the company?
questions.answer: Yes, they have the powers of a Civil Court to summon any person as a witness.

questions.question: What if the witness refuses to cooperate?
questions.answer: The IC can report this to the employer for disciplinary action.

questions.question: Is the IC bound by the "Indian Evidence Act"?
questions.answer: No, they follow the principles of Natural Justice, which are more flexible.

questions.question: What is "Victimization" during an inquiry?
questions.answer: Any adverse action (bad appraisal, isolation) taken against the woman for filing the complaint.

questions.question: Can the IC ask about the woman’s sexual history?
questions.answer: Absolutely not; it is irrelevant to the case.

questions.question: How are "Minutes of the Meeting" handled?
questions.answer: They must be recorded and signed by all present members and the parties.

questions.question: What is "Circumstantial Evidence"?
questions.answer: Indirect evidence (logs, gate entries, mood changes) that supports a claim.

questions.question: Can the IC order a lie-detector test?
questions.answer: No, they do not have the power for forensic criminal testing.

questions.question: Who bears the cost of the inquiry?
questions.answer: The employer.

questions.question: What if the IC discovers a criminal offense?
questions.answer: They must assist the woman if she chooses to file a police report.

questions.question: Can the PO (Presiding Officer) be changed mid-way?
questions.answer: Only in exceptional cases like resignation or bias.

questions.question: Is a "He-said/She-said" case automatically dismissed?
questions.answer: No; the IC must weigh the credibility of both parties and look for indirect evidence.

questions.question: Can the IC take "Suo Moto" action?
questions.answer: No, they cannot start an inquiry without a formal complaint.

questions.question: What happens to the interim leave granted?
questions.answer: It is in addition to the leaves the woman is already entitled to.

questions.question: Does the IC have to meet daily?
questions.answer: No, they schedule hearings based on the availability of parties and witnesses.

questions.question: Who can request conciliation?
questions.answer: Only the aggrieved woman.

questions.question: Can the IC force the parties to settle?
questions.answer: No; conciliation must be entirely voluntary.

questions.question: Can a monetary settlement be part of conciliation?
questions.answer: No, the Act strictly prohibits money-based settlements.

questions.question: What kind of settlements are allowed?
questions.answer: Apologies, changes in reporting structure, or counseling for the respondent.

questions.question: Does a successful conciliation lead to an inquiry?
questions.answer: No; the matter is closed once the settlement is recorded.

questions.question: What happens if the respondent violates the settlement?
questions.answer: The woman can ask the IC to revive the inquiry.

questions.question: To whom does the IC send the conciliation report?
questions.answer: To the Employer, the Complainant, and the Respondent.

questions.question: Is the "External Member" required for conciliation?
questions.answer: Yes, the IC must be fully constituted.

questions.question: Can the employer intervene in a conciliation?
questions.answer: No, the process is handled solely by the IC.

questions.question: Is conciliation mandatory before an inquiry?
questions.answer: No, it is an optional choice given to the woman.

questions.question: What if the woman changes her mind during conciliation?
questions.answer: She can stop the process and opt for a formal inquiry.

questions.question: Does the IC give a "finding" in conciliation?
questions.answer: No; they only record the mutually agreed terms.

questions.question: Is a conciliation report confidential?
questions.answer: Yes, the same secrecy rules apply as an inquiry.

questions.question: Can the respondent request conciliation?
questions.answer: No, the law gives this right only to the woman.

questions.question: What is the timeframe for conciliation?
questions.answer: It should ideally be wrapped up quickly to avoid delaying a potential inquiry.

questions.question: How long does the IC have to submit the Final Report?
questions.answer: 10 days after completing the inquiry.

questions.question: What if the allegations are NOT proven?
questions.answer: The IC recommends that no action be taken.

questions.question: What if the complaint is found to be "Malicious"?
questions.answer: The IC can recommend action against the complainant as per company service rules.

questions.question: Is "Inability to Prove" the same as a "False Complaint"?
questions.answer: No; a complaint is only malicious if there is intent to deceive.

questions.question: What punishments can the IC recommend for the Respondent?
questions.answer: Warning, fine, withholding promotion, counseling, or termination.

questions.question: How is "Compensation" calculated?
questions.answer: Based on mental trauma, medical expenses, loss of career, and the respondent's income.

questions.question: Can the employer ignore the IC’s recommendation?
questions.answer: No; the employer must act on the recommendation within 60 days.

questions.question: Can the IC recommend a police FIR?
questions.answer: Yes, if the act is a criminal offense under the Indian Penal Code (or BNS).

questions.question: Who can appeal against the IC’s decision?
questions.answer: Either party (Complainant or Respondent).

questions.question: Where is an appeal filed?
questions.answer: In a court or tribunal as per service rules, within 90 days.

questions.question: Does a "warning" count as a punishment?
questions.answer: Yes, it is a formal disciplinary action.

questions.question: What if the respondent is a high-performer?
questions.answer: Performance is irrelevant; the IC must judge based on the harassment evidence.

questions.question: Can the IC recommend "Community Service"?
questions.answer: Yes, if the company policy allows it for minor misconduct.

questions.question: Can the compensation be deducted from the respondent’s salary?
questions.answer: Yes, the employer is authorized to do so.

questions.question: What if the respondent has left the company?
questions.answer: The IC still submits the report; the employer can mark "not for re-hire" or withhold dues.

questions.question: What is the "Reasoned Order"?
questions.answer: A report that clearly explains why the IC reached its conclusion.

questions.question: Can the IC recommend that the respondent apologize in public?
questions.answer: No; apologies should be handled privately to maintain confidentiality.

questions.question: Is a "Transfer" a punishment?
questions.answer: It can be a recommendation to prevent further contact.

questions.question: Can the IC recommend a fine for a false witness?
questions.answer: Yes, they can recommend disciplinary action.

questions.question: What if the employer fails to act on the report?
questions.answer: They face a fine of up to ₹50,000 and possible cancellation of their business license.

questions.question: What is the fine for an employer’s first non-compliance?
What happens on a second non-compliance?
questions.answer: The fine is doubled, and business licenses or registrations may be cancelled.

questions.question: Is a written POSH Policy mandatory?
questions.answer: Yes, every organization with 10+ employees must have one.

questions.question: Where should the IC members' names be displayed?
questions.answer: In a conspicuous place in the office (e.g., notice boards).

questions.question: When is the POSH Annual Report due?
questions.answer: Usually by January 31st for the previous calendar year.

questions.question: To whom is the Annual Report submitted?
questions.answer: To the District Officer (DO) and the Employer.

questions.question: What must the Annual Report include?
questions.answer: Number of complaints received, disposed of, pending for 90+ days, and awareness sessions held.

questions.question: Is a "Nil Report" required?
questions.answer: Yes, even if there were zero complaints, a report must be filed.

questions.question: How often must awareness programs be held?
questions.answer: Regularly; at least once or twice a year for all employees.

questions.question: Is "Gender Sensitization" training mandatory?
questions.answer: Yes, it is a key preventive obligation of the employer.

questions.question: Must the employer provide a safe working environment?
questions.answer: Yes, this includes preventing third-party harassment.

questions.question: Does the employer have to assist in filing a police report?
questions.answer: Yes, if the woman chooses to do so.

questions.question: Is there a "National SHe-Box"?
questions.answer: Yes, it is a central portal by the Ministry of Women and Child Development for reporting.

questions.question: Should POSH compliance be mentioned in the Board’s Report?
questions.answer: Yes, under the Companies Act, listed companies must disclose this.

questions.question: Who is responsible for training the IC members?
questions.answer: The Employer.

questions.question: Scenario: A colleague follows a woman on Instagram and likes every old photo. POSH?
questions.answer: If it makes her uncomfortable and is unwelcome, it can be considered "stalking" and "non-verbal harassment."

questions.question: Scenario: Harassment happens at a client’s office. Who investigates?
questions.answer: The woman’s own employer's IC should investigate, with cooperation from the client’s office.

questions.question: Scenario: An employee is harassed by a food delivery person in the office cafeteria. POSH?
questions.answer: Yes, it is "Third-party harassment." The employer must take action to ban the person and assist the victim.

questions.question: Scenario: A manager asks a team member for a "private dinner" to discuss her promotion. POSH?
questions.answer: Yes, this is a "Quid Pro Quo" situation.

questions.question: Scenario: An employee displays a suggestive desktop wallpaper. POSH?
questions.answer: Yes, this creates a "Hostile Work Environment."

questions.question: Scenario: "Office Gossip" about a woman's character. POSH?
questions.answer: Yes, it falls under verbal conduct of a sexual nature that creates a hostile environment.

questions.question: Scenario: A man is harassed by a woman. Can the IC reject it?
questions.answer: Under the POSH Act, yes. However, under a "Gender Neutral" company policy, they should investigate.

questions.question: Scenario: Two employees are in a consensual relationship that turns sour. POSH?
questions.answer: Only if one party begins harassing the other after the relationship ends.

questions.question: Scenario: An incident occurs at a "Work from Home" location. POSH?
questions.answer: Yes, the home is an "extended workplace" during work hours.

questions.question: Scenario: Harassment via an anonymous "fake" profile. POSH?
questions.answer: The IC can investigate if the harasser can be identified as an employee (e.g., via IT logs).

questions.question: Scenario: A client sends lewd messages on LinkedIn. POSH?
questions.answer: Yes, the employer must assist the employee and can terminate the client relationship.

questions.question: Scenario: Touching a colleague’s hair and calling it "friendly." POSH?
questions.answer: If it is unwelcome by the recipient, it is harassment.

questions.question: Scenario: "Man-splaining" or regular yelling. POSH?
questions.answer: Not necessarily sexual harassment (it’s general misconduct) unless it has a sexual undertone.

questions.question: Scenario: An employee is harassed in the office lift. POSH?
questions.answer: Yes, it is within the workplace premises.

questions.question: Scenario: A manager comments on a woman's pregnancy in a derogatory sexual way. POSH?
questions.answer: Yes, this is a sexually colored remark.

questions.question: Scenario: A group of men share "adult" jokes in the presence of a woman colleague. POSH?
questions.answer: Yes, it creates a "Hostile Work Environment."

questions.question: Scenario: An employee complains about harassment that happened 2 years ago. POSH?
questions.answer: Technically barred by the 3+3 month rule, but the IC can look into it for "general safety" concerns.

questions.question: Scenario: A woman is harassed at a conference in another city. POSH?
questions.answer: Yes, it is an "extended workplace."

questions.question: Scenario: A colleague asks for a date once, she says no, and he never asks again. POSH?
questions.answer: Likely not harassment, as it wasn't persistent or severe enough to be "unwelcome" in a legal sense.

questions.question: Scenario: A witness is afraid to testify due to the respondent's power. IC action?
questions.answer: The IC must offer protection and can allow written statements.

questions.question: Scenario: The IC leaked the complainant's name. Penalty?
questions.answer: The leaking member must be removed, and the employer can be fined.

questions.question: Scenario: A contractor is harassed by a full-time employee. POSH?
questions.answer: Yes, she is an "Aggrieved Woman" under the Act.

questions.question: Scenario: Sending a "Red Heart" emoji to a subordinate. POSH?
questions.answer: In a professional context, this is often considered inappropriate and potentially unwelcome.

questions.question: Scenario: A respondent resigns as soon as the complaint is filed. IC action?
questions.answer: The inquiry continues to its logical end to record the findings.

questions.question: Scenario: A woman is harassed in a company-sponsored marathon. POSH?
questions.answer: Yes, it is an official event organized by the employer.
